finds.what: Append-only SQLite world: one call runs the whole admission (fragment gate -> wrap_scene -> pinned XSD 4.0 + semantic) and commits a hash-chained entry with compare-and-swap on head/tail. append(candidate={title,instruction,x3d,generator}) accepts an external fragment, so a Weaver output can go in directly. Rejected tries are written to an append-only attempts table. UPDATE/DELETE triggers keep both tables immutable.
finds.how: Treat each flywheel turn as snap=store.snapshot(); store.append(expected_head=snap['head'], expected_tail_hash=snap['tail_hash'], candidate=weaver_out). The returned entry n is the turn count. Catch AdmissionRefused (its .attempt holds the stage-by-stage refusal for Keeper) and Conflict (retry). I ran a smoke test: an external <Shape><Box/></Shape> candidate committed as n=1 and verify() came back valid.
finds.needs: stdlib sqlite3 plus lxml==6.1.1 and jsonschema==4.26.0 for the validator stage. No network, API or GPU.

finds.what: Stdlib-only bounded-fragment gate (v2.0.0). It allows 24 node types plus ROUTE, typed and range-checked fields, DEF/USE/ROUTE namespacing under a caller prefix, and caps on bytes, nodes, depth, lights, timers and interpolators. It fits the fragment conservatively into a 3 m slot. It returns status, named GATE_* errors, canonical_x3d, canonical_sha256, raw_sha256, bounds, fit and metrics (including a 0-5 complexity score).
finds.how: Run it first as the cheap pre-check: gate_fragment(xml, prefix='A000123'). The GATE_* codes are machine-readable reasons that can go back to Weaver for a fix-and-retry loop with no model, or to the Haiku allowance. Use metrics.complexity to rank candidates.
finds.needs: Python stdlib only (xml.etree). No network, API or GPU.

finds.what: Deterministic authored procedural sculpture generator: 6 families (orrery, coral, ziggurat, beacon, mycelium, gyroscope), 4 palettes, tiers 1-5, with TimeSensor, OrientationInterpolator and ColorInterpolator animation. It never calls a model and reports model_calls: 0. A review sent 1200 seeded candidates through the full pipeline with 0 failures.
finds.how: This is the no-model default. Map a Scout signal to seed_word (WORD_FAMILIES maps 'orbit', 'reef', 'lighthouse', 'forest' and similar words to a family) and pass the plan from world.plan_next. The wheel turns even when the daily allowance is zero. WorldStore.append(candidate=None) calls it automatically.
finds.needs: Stdlib only. No network, API or GPU.

finds.what: Offline calls into the vendored, hash-pinned x3d_mcp validator (hagopjay/x3d_mcp@b5c9956): XSD 4.0 plus semantic diagnostics. It re-checks the vendored file hashes against ORIGIN.json on every call and fails closed on drift. A missing dependency is an explicit not_run, never a fake pass. candidate_sha256 binds the verdict to the exact bytes.
finds.how: Call validate_scene(world.wrap_scene(fragment)) as the second instrument. Keeper stores the instrument block (repository, commit, code_sha256) as witness provenance. This is the 'x3d_mcp fork validator' stage, ready to use with no MCP server process.
finds.needs: lxml and jsonschema, plus the vendor/x3d_mcp tree (already vendored). No network.

finds.what: 40-line stdlib canonical JSON (accretion-c14n/1): sorted keys, integral floats normalized, NaN, Infinity and duplicate keys refused. It also provides the sha256 helper used for every hash in the chain.
finds.how: Copy or import it for the Gobbler ledger, so Gobbler hashes use the same bytes as accretion entries and one chain can cite the other's entry_hash. It is also the strict parser for any Haiku JSON output.
finds.needs: Stdlib only.

finds.what: Offline archive verifier. It checks genesis, sequence and prev-hash links, payload digests, deterministic placement replay, candidate byte digests, policy digest and witness binding, plus an optional HEAD:HASH checkpoint. export_x3d_from_archive merges every admitted fragment into one Immersive X3D 4.0 scene, with a Viewpoint and light, ready to view.
finds.how: After each turn, run verify_export.py world.json --checkpoint HEAD:HASH in the GitHub Actions job, using the previous run's committed checkpoint.json. Write export.x3d as the growing world artifact. The checkpoint closes the truncation gap (review L1).
finds.needs: Stdlib for verification. No network.

finds.what: Turns a verified archive into a deterministic, server-less, read-only site payload (web/static-world/api/*.json, patches/NNNNNN.x3d, export.x3d, manifest.json). The X_ITE web viewer and an in-browser Web Crypto port of verify_archive (Node and browser) come with it. --check mode fails CI when the payload is stale.
finds.how: At the end of each Actions run, call export_static.py --archive world.json and publish web/ to GitHub Pages, so every admitted turn appears in a public 3D viewer. That is where the flywheel is visible. The demo-96 payload is already built.
finds.needs: Python stdlib. Pages hosting is free. The viewer needs WebGL in the reader's browser.

finds.what: Deterministic placement planner. The seed is sha(prev_hash:n). It chooses generate (a new spiral cell) or augment (stack a level on a recent cell, up to 5 levels), and a biome by ring. A review replay of 10,000 turns gave 0 collisions.
finds.how: Use it to decide each turn's slot and seed before Weaver runs. A signal can force_mode='augment' or 'generate'. The plan's seed_word and biome feed generate() or a Haiku prompt.
finds.needs: Stdlib only.

finds.what: Normalized witness summary (fragment, xsd, semantic, render) with status, instrument and scope for each entry. The render stage is already a not_run, required=False slot. Each attempt record lists its stages with their status and detail.
finds.how: Source for the foldback notes to x3d.docs and x3d.loom: count refusals by GATE_* code across attempts to find vocabulary gaps (for example PhysicalMaterial, review F1). The X_ITE render probe from Witness fills the render row.
finds.needs: Stdlib only.

finds.what: Working GitHub Actions template: Python 3.12 and 3.13 matrix, pip install of requirements, unittest, node --check on the JS, a static-payload freshness check and archive verification. I ran the local suite: 99 tests OK in 4.3 s.
finds.how: Copy it as the skeleton for the 30-minute schedule job: add a cron trigger, a turn step, verify, export_static, then commit and push the archive and checkpoint (contents: write).
finds.needs: GitHub Actions (free tier). No secrets for the no-model path.

finds.what: build_demo grows N entries (1-512) through the real pipeline in a temporary SQLite database and writes the public archive, checkpoint and admission summary. benchmark_store measures append, replay and export cost at 10, 100 and 1000 entries.
finds.how: build_demo is the reference loop for a 'turn' (DB to archive). Its archive-writing code is the pattern for persisting state between ephemeral Actions runs. Use benchmark_store to size how many turns fit in one run's budget (about 30-40 ms per append at 100 entries).
finds.needs: lxml and jsonschema. No network.

finds.what: The exact admitted vocabulary, field list, ROUTE graph rules and caps table (12 KiB raw, 80 nodes, 12 routes, 8 interpolators, 2-32 keys, 1 local light and so on).
finds.how: Paste it, or a compressed copy, into the Haiku system prompt so that model-written fragments target what the gate admits, and into the Keeper foldback notes. It also serves as a deterministic checklist for a template-based Weaver.
finds.needs: None.

finds.what: Stdlib fail-closed primitives: need() raises GateError(code) instead of assert, so it still works under python -O; candidate() gives a sha256 inventory of a whole tree (excludes evidence/.git/node_modules); write_witness() writes one loom.witness/1 record bound to that candidate and refuses with CANDIDATE_CHANGED_DURING_WITNESS if the tree changed mid-run; status and grade are kept separate (pass/fail/error/not_run/deferred x C/L/S); canonical() gives deterministic JSON bytes.
finds.how: Copy or vendor kit/loomkit (stdlib, Python 3.10+). Every Witness probe (x3d_mcp validator, X_ITE probe, accrete gate_fragment) writes its result through write_witness() into RUN/evidence/<name>.json, with the turn's candidate sha as subject. canonical()+sha256_bytes give Keeper deterministic hashes for its chain links.
finds.needs: Nothing: stdlib only, no network, API or GPU

finds.what: Acceptance by named profile, never by a score: loads a loom.profile/1 JSON with the required witnesses, then checks for each one that a record exists, its schema is right, it is bound to the current candidate (STALE_WITNESS), it is not development, its status is allowed, a pass is grade C, coverage matches and the evidence files' hashes match (EVIDENCE_DRIFT). Returns an acceptance summary or raises with a stable code.
finds.how: This is the supervisor's admit/reject decision for one flywheel turn. Write a gobbler-turn/v1 profile (required: grammar, meaning, traps, accrete-gate, xite-probe with allow:[deferred]) like kit/profiles/x3d-static.json. Call acc.accept(candidate_root, evidence_dir, profile). Only on 'accepted' does the turn count and WorldStore get the fragment.
finds.needs: Nothing: stdlib, offline

finds.what: loom.receipt/1 builder. Fields: subject, candidate sha, a hash of every witness record, outputs with bytes and sha256, not_run, model_calls, budget, and prev (the sha256 of the previous receipt file), self-hashed over canonical JSON. write() refuses to overwrite (RECEIPT_EXISTS). verify() catches RECEIPT_DRIFT. Unsigned on purpose (law 35).
finds.how: Keeper's hash-chained ledger entry for each admitted turn: call receipt.build(..., model_calls=[haiku calls with prompt sha], budget={'haiku_tokens_used':..,'allowance':..}, prev=last_receipt) and then receipt.write(). The prev link is the chain. Use build() directly, because the CLI path (cli.py ~L287) hard-codes budget paid_calls=0. Flywheel turn count = length of the receipt chain. Trap: verify() checks one receipt only. There is no walker over the whole chain, so Keeper must write a short loop that checks each prev hash.
finds.needs: Nothing: stdlib, offline

finds.what: File-only, stdlib X3D trap scanner with 15 rules. Each rule names the incident that paid for it and is labelled with the runtime it was seen on (any vs X_ITE 16.5.1). Rules include shader-raw-source, route-before-def, route-undefined, color-range, splat-bbox, movie-not-still, version-fits-nodes (4.1-only nodes in a 4.0 file), metadata-containerfield, glsl-reserved-active, color-keys-sparse, xite-light-zero-pop and xite-transparent-shadow. check(bytes, {'host':...}) returns Hit(rule, severity, where, detail).
finds.how: Cheap first witness on each Weaver fragment, before the slower validator or the X_ITE probe: traps.check(fragment_bytes, {'host':'strict'}). An error-level hit rejects the fragment straight away. The stable rule ids also give Scout/Weaver a vocabulary of known X_ITE pitfalls to match news against (for example a new X_ITE release changes a runtime-labelled rule).
finds.needs: Nothing: stdlib, offline

finds.what: Wrapper that runs the x3d_mcp fork's validate_xml + semantic_diagnostics in a subprocess using the fork's own venv, read-only. Records the fork commit, branch and dirty flag as instrument identity. A missing fork or venv is an InstrumentError (status error), never a pass. summarise() reduces the output to xsd_valid, error counts and semantic warnings.
finds.how: The exact call shape for the 'x3d_mcp fork validator' step. Set LOOM_FORK=/home/user/x3d_mcp (or the Actions checkout path) and give it a venv. grammar.validate([paths]) feeds two witnesses, grammar and meaning, both bound to the fork commit (law 15).
finds.needs: An x3d_mcp checkout with .venv/bin/python and its deps (lxml etc.); git. No network at run time. TRAP: the default path is ~/Projects/x3d/x3d_mcp, and /home/user/x3d_mcp has no .venv right now, so it will raise InstrumentError on CI until the workflow builds the venv.

finds.what: Trust tier for free text, stdlib. lint_text() runs 10 blunt regexes for injection-like patterns (override-instructions, role-reassign, system-prompt, answer-steering, suppress-report, self-grading, ...). quote_untrusted() applies NFKC normalisation, strips control and bidi characters, caps length, hashes, and withholds flagged text.
finds.how: Run every scraped web snippet (release notes, forum posts, X3D news) through quote_untrusted() before it enters a signal record or any Haiku prompt. Flagged items are kept as hash + flags only. This also covers MetadataString/WorldInfo text in fragments Weaver proposes. The README is explicit that this is not a prompt-injection guarantee.
finds.needs: Nothing: stdlib, offline (239 pytest tests pass for x3d.s1 in a copy; pytest is test-only)

finds.what: Model-call boundary with no network of its own. HostedAdapter(transport, model) builds the request and takes an injected transport callable. It refuses unpinned or alias model ids (latest/preview/...), checks that the served model equals the requested one, and fails closed on malformed responses. Also provides estimate_input_tokens / estimate_cost_usd / check_limits before any call, ReplayBackend (recorded answers; an unknown id raises) and StubBackend. Plus questions.py (typed Choice/Score/Noul answers with probabilities) and routing.py (policy -> suspected_ok | escalate_oracle | defer_human).
finds.how: Fits the 'default no model, Haiku under a small typed daily allowance' rule: run with ReplayBackend/StubBackend by default. Only when the allowance permits, inject a Claude Haiku transport. Count estimate_input_tokens against the daily allowance before the call and refuse when over. route_choice decides whether a Haiku answer may stay advisory (S) or must escalate to the validator. decidable.py questions are answered by code and never asked, which saves allowance.
finds.needs: Offline as shipped. A Haiku transport would need an API key plus a small adapter. TRAP: the price and token constants (LIST_PRICE_USD_PER_MTOK_INPUT=0.042, 64k/32k limits) and the request wire shape are for a different vendor's 'jev' model, not Anthropic. Do not reuse those numbers for Haiku.

finds.what: Fold-back witness: parses a patch (git or unified), checks it is additions-only, runs git apply --check in an empty temp repo, then runs every tools/<name>/smoke.py under python and python -O. Distinguishes fail from error (missing dependency). Paired with kit/templates/FOLDBACK-FORM.md, the PR-body template (summary, apply/test, additions table, rules proposed with diagnostic and blind spots).
finds.how: Keeper drafts foldback notes to x3d.loom and x3d.docs as additions-only patches in this shape and checks them with foldback.check(patch) before saving the draft. It never sends them (law 16: nothing leaves without 'send'). kit/examples/check_all_foldbacks.py shows the batch loop, grouping copies by sha256.
finds.needs: git and python only; offline

finds.what: Headless X_ITE stills harness. A tiny static server with correct MIME types (.css must be text/css or the canvas goes blank) runs Chromium on SwiftShader with one fresh context per still. glspy.js (injected before page scripts) counts draw calls, program links and shader compiles and keeps the first compile/link error logs. Prints one JSON line per still (load ms, compile counts, console errors). fetch_xite.sh pins X_ITE 16.5.1 via npm pack and prints its sha256.
finds.how: Base for the X_ITE render probe. Load each candidate world at accrete-turn N, then require zero shader-compile errors and zero console errors, and a non-blank still as evidence (a sha256 written via write_witness). Use the counters as the probe's measurements. Software GL only: never report frame rates. Free on GitHub Actions ubuntu runners with Playwright.
finds.needs: Node + Playwright + Chromium download, plus npm registry access for X_ITE at fetch time. No GPU (SwiftShader). Note: pinned to 16.5.1 while x3d.accrete bundles 16.6.0, so align the pin.

finds.what: Picture-review protocol validator for a model judge. The review must be bound to the candidate sha and each frame's sha256. Every flag has a normalised region, a concern of more than 15 chars and state 'suspected'. Numeric scores or ratings are rejected by regex (PICTURE_GRADING), and promotion to truth is rejected (MODEL_TRUTH_PROMOTION).
finds.how: If the daily allowance spends a Haiku call looking at an X_ITE still, run its JSON through picture.validate(review, subject_sha, frames) before storing it. The result is always grade S, advisory, and never a required witness for admission (laws 6 and 9).
finds.needs: Nothing to validate. Producing the review would need Haiku (paid, optional).

finds.what: Leak sweep (law 16): copies a tree, applies ordered regex replacements from a loom.sweep-rules/1 file, then fails if any forbidden pattern survives anywhere (binary files too). Writes loom.sweep-report/1 (see /home/user/x3d.loom/SWEEP-REPORT.json: 67 replacements, residue [] , status pass).
finds.how: Run on every foldback draft and on the public ledger or world export before commit or publish from GitHub Actions. That keeps home paths, session links and key-shaped strings out of public repos. The sweep report hash can go in the receipt.
finds.needs: Stdlib. TRAP: the rules file kit/profiles/public-sweep.json, named in the docstring and the CLI help, is NOT in kit/profiles, so Keeper must write its own rules file.

finds.what: LLM co-editor op vocabulary: modify_node / add_node / remove_node / move_node against DEF names, the same ops as x3d_mcp src/tools/scene_ops.py. agentApply validates that each DEF exists and returns a result per op. A hallucinated DEF gets an error back instead of corrupting the doc. Backed by the yx3d.js CRDT model (setField, addXML, addRoute, toXML), plus a Python peer on pycrdt.
finds.how: Use AGENT_TOOLS as Weaver's typed output schema for 'proposed change' (one add_node op with an X3D fragment = one accrete addition). The op list is small enough for constrained output under Haiku and also writable by deterministic templates. Later the growing world can be a shared Yjs doc so humans and the Gobbler co-edit it.
finds.needs: Node + yjs 13.6.33 (npm). The Python peer needs pycrdt. No API needed.

finds.what: gate(xml) returns {valid, errors, hints, stage}: XSD first, then error-level semantic diagnostics, and each error comes with a fix you can apply mechanically (op/path/attribute/value). repair_with_hints(xml, max_steps=30) applies those fixes one by one and re-gates after each, returning {fixed, valid, applied, remaining_errors}. No model involved. I checked it by hand: a Box with containerField='children' fails the gate, one 'wrong-containerfield' fix is applied, and the result is valid.
finds.how: Witness uses gate() as the admit/reject verdict for each candidate fragment. When the gate fails, Weaver runs repair_with_hints() before it reaches for the Haiku allowance, so many turns finish with no model call. Keeper writes the 'applied' list into the ledger as the repair trail.
finds.needs: lxml only (no network, API or GPU). Import validation.hints directly and never tools.*. It loads schemas/verified-containment.json, the X3DUOM and validation.semantic._type_ancestry, so the x3d.accrete vendored subset (which has validate.py and semantic.py only) would need hints.py and those data files added to ORIGIN.json.

finds.what: The in-process XSD validator (4.0/4.1 schemas bundled; version picked from the document or given as an argument) and roughly 30 structured semantic checks (DEF/USE, ROUTE types, containerField, profile components, tuple counts, interpolator keys, colour range, HAnim names, index bounds) returned as Diagnostic dataclasses with level/check/message. tests/test_inprocess_signatures.py locks the signatures as append-only. x3d.accrete already vendors these at commit b5c9956, and git log shows no changes to either file between b5c9956 and HEAD fa5dccf, so the pin is current.
finds.how: Call validate_xml(xml, version='4.0') and then semantic_diagnostics(xml), as /home/user/x3d.accrete/accretion/mcp_adapter.py already does. A fragment passes when the XSD is valid and there are no error-level diagnostics. Keep warning and info counts as flywheel telemetry.
finds.needs: lxml and jsonschema (validate.py imports jsonschema even for XML). No network, API or GPU. The parser is set to no_network and resolve_entities=False.

finds.what: A hash-chained JSON Lines claim ledger. Each record is canonical JSON with claim, grade (Confirmed/Likely/Suspected), subject, instrument, evidence, prev and sha256. append(text, {...}, chain=True) links the new record to the previous one; verify(rows, chain=True) reports broken hashes or links and the chain head; page() returns slimmed slices with hashes dropped or shortened. Standard library only. Checked by hand: two appends, then verify gave ok=True with a head hash.
finds.how: Keeper can copy this as the ledger: one record per admitted flywheel turn (subject = fragment sha, instrument = validator commit + X_ITE version, evidence = gate output digest). verify(chain=True) runs at the start of every Actions run, and the turn count is records + head. The grade vocabulary already matches the Confirmed/Likely/Suspected scale used here.
finds.needs: Standard library only (hashlib, json). No network.

finds.what: Puts one known defect into a valid scene (route typo or type, dropped or duplicate DEF, unknown field, bad bool, version or profile drift, missing geometry, keyValue count, plus the 'silent' faults invisible and camera_away that only a render can catch). catalogue() says which layer should catch each one.
finds.how: A canary run on every turn: mutate the newly admitted fragment with each operator and check that the gate (or the render probe, for the silent faults) rejects it. This shows the gate still bites, which is cheap evidence Keeper can log with each turn and stops the flywheel from 'turning' through a gate that has gone dead.
finds.needs: lxml only. No network. It lives under playground/, so copy the file rather than importing the package, because playground/__init__ pulls in config and auth.

finds.what: Deterministic repair. It fixes containerField, header drift (missing profile or version, raising the version to the lowest one that contains every node), missing <component> statements, xsi namespace and DEF-before-USE ordering among siblings, then re-validates. It returns {fixed, changes, unfixable, remaining} with a reason for each change.
finds.how: Weaver applies it after generating a template or Haiku fragment and before handing it to Witness, especially when the world's profile or components must grow to take a new node type. The changes list becomes the 'what the validator changed' line in the foldback note to x3d.loom.
finds.needs: lxml and jsonschema, no network. test_repair::test_x3dpy_https_xsi_namespace_corrected fails without the 'x3d' (x3d.py) package. In my run that was the 1 failure out of 384 tests.

finds.what: Headless X_ITE 16.4.3 render to PNG in Chromium with software WebGL (swiftshader), serving the scene over a loopback HTTP server. analyze_frame(png) classifies the frame as blank, sparse or ok, with the non-background fraction, background colour and bbox. frame_warning() explains likely causes (viewer fell under WALK, camera facing away, clipping, unlit). .github/workflows/tests.yml already has a 'render smoke (Chromium)' job running this on ubuntu-latest.
finds.how: Render probe: draw the accreted world after each admission. Reject or flag the turn if analyze_frame reports 'blank'. Use the change in bbox or non_background_fraction between turns as visible proof that the world grew. Keeper attaches the PNG sha to the ledger record. Copy the helpers, because tools/render.py imports mcp.server.fastmcp at module level.
finds.needs: playwright plus chromium (heavy; cache it in Actions), pillow for analyze_frame. Network to the jsdelivr CDN unless X3D_MCP_XITE_JS points at a local x_ite.min.js. CPU only, no GPU.

finds.what: Downloads the pinned X_ITE release tarball, checks it against a pinned SHA-256 (16.4.3: f3a28140...) and unpacks only x_ite.min.js, x_ite.css, LICENSE and assets/. Standard library only.
finds.how: Run it once per Actions cache key so render probes use a hash-verified local X_ITE (set X3D_MCP_XITE_JS to a loopback URL). Every render verdict then names an exact renderer, and Keeper can store that in the instrument field.
finds.needs: Network once (registry.npmjs tarball), then offline. Standard library only.

finds.what: A lexical expat inspector that never reserialises and refuses custom entities. audit_scene(bytes) gives byte-located witnesses for duplicate DEF, unresolved, forward or wrong-type USE and dangling ROUTE endpoints, bound to source_sha256. patch_attribute(source, def_name=, attribute=, value=, expected_sha256) changes exactly one attribute and keeps every other byte, refusing a stale hash or an ambiguous DEF.
finds.how: Weaver proposes small x3d.loom changes as patch_attribute edits guarded by the current world's sha, so concurrent or stale turns cannot clobber the world. Before a merge, Witness runs audit_scene on world + fragment to catch DEF name collisions between the new fragment and the existing WorldStore.
finds.needs: Standard library only (expat, hashlib, hmac). No network.

finds.what: A budgeted (budget_bytes hard cap), trust-tiered JSON digest of a scene: node counts, world-space bounds, camera, lights, ROUTE counts, validator verdicts. Author text (DEF names, meta, urls, Script) is never echoed, only counted and hashed. That makes it safe to feed to a model even when content came from the web.
finds.how: Keeper puts a before/after brief of the growing world into the foldback note and the ledger evidence (bounds and node counts show the flywheel turning). Weaver passes a roughly 1 KB brief, not the whole world, to Haiku when the allowance is spent, which keeps tokens small and resists prompt injection.
finds.needs: lxml. No network. Use x3d_utils.scene_brief, not tools/scene_brief.py (which needs mcp).

finds.what: Value-level evidence: for each claimed value with a short quote, FIND (is the quote in the source text), COMPARE (is the value in the quote: numbers, vectors, colours, units) and LOCATE (span, line and column, X3D node or DEF path). scene_evidence adds BIND (does the scene actually hold that value). It returns verdicts and offsets, never the quotes. x3dtrace is standard library only.
finds.how: Scout stores the fetched article text as a source. When Weaver turns a signal into a fragment value (a new field default, a colour, a dimension), scene_evidence checks the value is quoted from the article and present in the fragment. Keeper records a verdict of 'verified' or 'unsupported' as the turn's provenance grade.
finds.needs: x3dtrace: standard library only. scene_evidence: lxml. No network beyond Scout's own fetch. Note that 'verified' only means the quote contains the value, not that the value is correct.

finds.what: Seeded, deterministic generators for IndexedFaceSet meshes (grid, sphere, torus), Extrusions (circle, star, polygon cross-sections) and interpolators, plus an X3DUOM-derived table of every valid (parent, field, containerField) placement for a node type, sorted so each page has stable bytes and a stable hash.
finds.how: The default no-model Weaver: on each turn, pick a generator with seed = turn number to produce one new geometry fragment, and use where_can_place to choose a legal parent and containerField in the world. Witness then gates it. This gives one guaranteed candidate per run even when Scout finds nothing.
finds.needs: numeric_sequences: standard library (math, random) plus dataset.schema.TrainingExample. placement: lxml and X3DUOM. No network. I did not check that the generator output passes the gate unchanged.

finds.what: full_report gives one structured layered verdict (xml, xsd, semantic, with stats, located errors and a repair preview). defects_for_prompt(report, limit) packs the defects into a compact list suitable for a prompt. restricted_schema(nodes) cuts the X3D JSON Schema down to a node subset for constrained model output.
finds.how: Witness can copy full_report's shape as its verdict document, and scene_hash as the fragment id. When the Haiku allowance is used, Weaver sends defects_for_prompt output, not raw errors, and asks for JSON constrained by restricted_schema, then converts it with x3d_utils.json2xml.json_to_xml before gating.
finds.needs: report.py: lxml and validation.*, no network. Copy it rather than importing playground. llm_schema: jsonschema data only. The Haiku call itself is the only API use.

finds.what: A stdlib state machine for the turn protocol: candidate -> reproduced -> guarded -> reused. A promotion needs evidence that is hash-bound and of the right kind: an observed-failure reproduction tied to the incident artifact, a guard with both a mutant-rejected and a valid-accepted control, and reuse only into a different domain with a bound scene input hash. Reuse is counted as distinct (guard, target, inputSha256) tuples, so running the same thing again adds no momentum. It raises ValueError on every illegal transition.
finds.how: Copy replay_incident as Keeper's 'admit a turn' predicate. Each Weaver proposal plus Witness runs becomes the artifacts and events lists, and verifiedReuses is the honest turn counter (repeating a run never inflates it). Use canonical_bytes plus sha256 for the ledger entry digests. Keep the 12-domain domain_manifest() as the allowed domain list, or swap it out.
finds.needs: Nothing. Stdlib, no network, no API, no GPU.

finds.path: /home/user/x3d.gobbler/flywheel-review/atlas/atlas.py (class Atlas: worklist, laws_for, what_broke, how_do_we_know, stands_on; --json)

finds.what: A copy of the x3d_mcp fork validator, unmodified and pinned to commit b5c9956 (XSD 4.0/4.1 plus semantic_diagnostics). finds.what: x3dprov 0.1, a hash-chained provenance record stored inside the X3D file's own <head><meta name='x3dprov.step.N'> lines. add_step(xml_before, step, xml_after) appends one step with prev, input_sha256 and output_sha256. content_hash() gives a C14N content hash with the provenance metas removed, and falls back to a text hash for XML that is not well-formed. verify() returns verified / stale / broken-chain / no-record with a list of problems. summary() lists the steps. 141 lines.
finds.how: On each admitted turn, call add_step() with a step such as {op:'accrete', turn:N, signal_id, weaver, witness_verdict, validator_sha} on the world file (or on each fragment). The world then carries its own ledger, and verify() becomes the start-of-run check that nothing was edited outside the flywheel ('stale'). Keeper's external hash-chained ledger can reuse _dumps (sorted keys, compact separators) and the prev = sha256(previous JSON) rule unchanged, so the two chains match.
finds.needs: No network, API or GPU. Needs lxml. No signing (tamper evidence only, not tamper proof).

finds.what: Spend ledger with hard caps. Budget(cap, path, parent, since, model): reserve() holds the call's worst-case cost before the call is made, so parallel workers cannot overshoot. charge() appends a JSONL row (t, utc, tag, model, in, out, usd) before the result is used. Budgets chain to a parent cap, and BudgetStop carries a scope. price() refuses any model with no listed price. summary() and markdown() print a cost table.
finds.how: Use it as the typed daily allowance for Claude Haiku. Set since = the start of the UTC day, a small cap, and a parent Budget for the month. Add Haiku to PRICES. Since an unlisted model is refused, a misconfigured model fails closed and the default stays 'no model'. The supervisor reserves before routing to Weaver's LLM path, and on BudgetStop it falls back to the deterministic path. Keeper commits ledger.jsonl and renders markdown() into the foldback note.
finds.needs: Stdlib only. No network.

finds.what: An X_ITE render probe, measured on 174 plus 358 scenes. measure(x) registers a callback on X_ITE's end-of-frame event before replaceWorld, so a blank scene cannot slip through by idling. It samples the canvas inside that callback and returns nonblank (the fraction of pixels that differ from the most common colour), frames, nodes, err and an 'Unknown node type' count. shot_nonblank() repeats the measure on a Playwright screenshot. Finding: a scene can be valid and still draw nothing (7 of 178 valid scenes were blank).
finds.how: Make it the 'visible' rung after the validator. Load the candidate world (world plus the new fragment) in headless Chromium/SwiftShader and require nonblank > 0, at least as high as the previous turn, and unknown == 0. The jpg thumbnail it already returns can be the visible frame for each turn. On GitHub Actions, npm install x_ite@16.5.0 and playwright, run mkxite.py to build xite/, and start serve.py.
finds.needs: No GPU (SwiftShader) and no API. Needs playwright, Pillow, Chromium and the X_ITE npm package. Network only for the install. The default GPU_PHASE_DIR is a private /mnt path; set RENDER_DIR. Expects serve.py on port 8782.

Copy the no-timestamp manifest convention so a replayed turn gives an identical hash. Copy reverify's idea to re-check that the world file on disk still matches the last ledger head. These are about 5 lines each, so copy them rather than import, because the add-on is GPL-3.
finds.needs: Nothing.

finds.what: A manifest-driven judge for X3D files using only the standard library. Cases are tiered CORE (FAIL, exit 1) or FIDELITY (WARN). It includes stdlib matrix, quaternion and slerp helpers, an interpolator integrity check (for example a short keyValue), and writes HTML, JSON and Markdown reports. '--selftest' passes; I ran it.

Its integrity checks (interpolator key/keyValue arity, world-transform maths) catch animated fragments that validate structurally but break at runtime. The Markdown report can feed Keeper's foldback.
finds.needs: Nothing (Python 3.9+, stdlib).

Store the identity_sha256 and report_sha256 in Keeper's ledger entry, so every admitted turn names the exact validator bytes that judged it. finds.what: Ways to change a live X_ITE scene without reloading the page. Chess creates nodes with createX3DFromString and pushes them into a persistent Group or addRootNode, with every update chained on one promise so async creates cannot interleave. particles.js adds a capped, short-lived ParticleSystem burst and then removes it. Mathslab guards replaceWorld with a revision counter so stale results are dropped, waits for x3d-canvas with a 7 s timeout, and falls back to 2D when WebGL is missing.

It then polls the ledger or world JSON and, for each new admitted turn, adds that one fragment as a child of a 'growth' Group through the serialized queue, with a particle burst at the fragment's anchor. A visitor watches the world grow by one piece per turn. Use replaceWorldInOrder for full re-syncs. Witness can reuse the same code inside a Playwright probe to confirm a fragment really inserts into the live world.

finds.what: A Playwright harness for X_ITE render probes. It serves a build dir the way the host does (only published files, .x3d as application/xml, a strict CSP copy on every response) and records console output, page errors, failed requests, HTTP errors and CSP violations, with a known-harmless list. eyes.mjs takes stills at fixed times and fails black, flat or blown-out frames (95th-percentile luminance thresholds).

finds.what: A stdlib-only, deterministic, bounded X3D 4.0 exporter (caps on primitives, points, indices and metadata bytes, with finite-number checks). It embeds the generating parameter card as canonical-JSON metadata inside the scene. card_from_x3d recovers that card under a 2 MiB budget, refuses DTD and ENTITY declarations and rejects duplicate keys, so a scene can be regenerated from its own metadata and compared.

Witness then runs card_from_x3d and regenerates the fragment. Byte-equal output proves the fragment is generator-made, not hand-edited. This works with no model at all.
finds.needs: No network, API or GPU. Python 3.11+ stdlib.

finds.what: A small deterministic X3D XML writer. Node(tag, kids, **attrs) keeps attributes in insertion order, num/mf apply one number-formatting rule, the document date comes from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (never the clock), MFString values are single-quoted safely, and output ends with exactly one newline. Same inputs give the same bytes.
finds.how: Use it to build fragments in Python so repeated runs every 30 minutes give identical bytes for identical inputs. Keeper can then dedupe proposals by sha256 and detect no-op turns.
finds.needs: No network, API or GPU. Stdlib only.

finds.what: A three-layer gate over a folder of .x3d files: the pinned fork validator, the Loom's loom_gate.py (11 trap rules, from x3d.onto gobbler-demiurge/tools), and five local stdlib trap rules with line numbers. Files listed in expect.json with must_fail are deliberately red, and a red fixture that comes out clean fails the run as a blind witness. In CI, pins.json is read and the validator and gate repos are checked out at exact commits.
finds.how: Copy the must_fail blind-fixture pattern so every Gobbler run proves the gate can still see. Copy the 'read pins, then actions/checkout at that ref' steps into the 30-minute Gobbler workflow so Witness always runs pinned tools. Add Gobbler-specific trap rules beside loomsong_rules.py as fragment-gate pre-checks.

finds.what: A stdlib receipt tool. 'write' runs a command under a fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and records the command, epoch, Python version, and the sha256 and size of every input and output. It refuses to overwrite an existing receipt without --force, because a receipt is a record, not a cache. 'check' re-hashes the inputs (stale if any changed), reruns the command and exits 1 on any output drift.
finds.how: For each admitted turn, Keeper writes a receipt for the Weaver command that produced the fragment, then chains receipt sha256 into the hash-chained ledger. A periodic 'check' job proves earlier turns still rebuild, which can count as a 'flywheel still true' metric.
finds.needs: No network, API or GPU. Stdlib only.

finds.what: A pre-publish sweep for API keys (Google, sk-, GitHub, AWS, Hugging Face), private keys, bearer tokens, service accounts, private links (claude.ai artifact links, Google Drive/Docs, gs://), AI vendor and model names, and costs. An optional out-of-repo private-strings file is supported, and a line can opt out with a 'sweep:allow RULE' marker. Exits 1 on any hit.
finds.how: Run it over every foldback note, ledger page and Scout-captured snippet before anything is committed or published from GitHub Actions. This stops a scraped page or a model output from leaking secrets into the public world.
finds.needs: No network, API or GPU. Stdlib only.

finds.how: After each turn, run release.py over the published world folder to bind exactly which bytes the front page serves. Put candidate_sha256 in the ledger and verify with --check before publishing. Render Keeper's foldback notes to x3d.loom and x3d.docs with report.py.

The chess ReplayTransport is a seeded, engine-free source that emits the same events as the live transports.

Use the ReplayTransport idea for a no-network demo mode: replay the ledger tape on the page with a seeded RNG so the flywheel can be shown turning even when no new turn was admitted.

finds.what: A beat tape {cycle, lub, dub, beats:[[interval, flag]]} that the front-page card describes as 'a replay of real validator runs'. It drives a visual pulse and a synthesized lub-dub scheduled against the clock's own phase.
finds.how: Keeper exports the ledger as a heart tape: one beat per turn, flag=1 for rejected or failed and 0 for admitted. The Gobbler page pulses with its real history, which makes the flywheel visibly turn. Only the tape format and HeartClock idea carry over; the WebGPU page itself does not.
finds.needs: No API. The tape is plain JSON. The original page needs WebGPU and Babylon from a CDN, so do not reuse the page.

finds.what: TimeSensor + interpolators + local ROUTE is the only behaviour X3D the gate admits. I probed it: a Transform spun by TimeSensor -> OrientationInterpolator -> ROUTE got status=pass. ROUTE endpoints must be DEFs inside the same patch, timer cycleInterval must be 0.5 to 3600 s, at most 32 keys.
finds.how: Use this as Weaver's 'motion' template so that each turn adds something visibly moving, and rotate through the four interpolator types. TimeSensor-driven replay of the ledger cannot live inside a fragment because ROUTEs are local only. It belongs in the world shell (see the export_x3d_from_archive find).
finds.needs: Nothing (stdlib Python)

finds.what: Builds the whole-world X3D 4.0 document from the hash-chained archive: one Transform per entry at plan.translation, wrapped in a shell that has WorldInfo, Background, Viewpoint and DirectionalLight. This shell is where all world-level X3D features belong, because fragments cannot carry them.
finds.how: Extend the shell, not the gate. Put WorldInfo info=[turn count, head hash]. Give each entry's Transform a MetadataSet name='turn' with MetadataString hash/prev_hash/created_utc/signal URL (the entry's DEF is turn_n). Add one Viewpoint per turn. Add a Switch whichChoice to show eras. Add a TimeSensor + ScalarInterpolator driving it for replay. All of this is computed from the archive, so it stays reproducible.
finds.needs: Nothing (stdlib)

A bounded number of Inline contexts is used. The X_ITE world view also adds WorldInfo, NavigationInfo, Fog and a DEF'd Viewpoint.
finds.how: Witness's X_ITE render probe can load exactly this makeWorld output. It gives you 'Inline per turn file' and 'LOD for a growing world' for free. A per-turn Anchor/Viewpoint could be added next to each LOD.
finds.needs: Browser + vendored X_ITE (no network)

I probed MetadataString, Switch and Text: each fails with GATE_NODE_FORBIDDEN. An X3D wrapper with version='4.1' fails with GATE_WRAPPER (only 4.0 is accepted).

HAnim could give agents an avatar, SpatialSound an audible 'turn chime', EnvironmentLight IBL, ParticleSystem an admission burst, InstancedShape (4.1) cheap repetition of past turns, GeoLocation anchors for Scout's news signals, and CADAssembly a 'part tree' per era. traps: SQLite world does not persist on GitHub Actions: WorldStore keeps state in a .db file and there is no import-from-archive function (only archive() export). Each 30-minute run must either commit the .db (binary churn) or write a small importer that re-INSERTs archive rows (INSERT is allowed; the triggers block only UPDATE and DELETE). Placement replay depends on the full history, so state cannot be dropped.

Instrument drift guards: WorldStore hashes every accretion/*.py plus serve.py at construction, gate.py and mcp_adapter.py hash themselves at import, and the adapter re-hashes vendor/x3d_mcp on every call. Editing or patching any of them inside a long-lived Flyte worker makes admission fail until restart. Vendor x3d.accrete read-only and pinned; do not modify it in place.

verify_archive checks self-consistency, not a fresh validator run (review L1). A forged but self-consistent entry, or a truncated archive, passes without an externally kept checkpoint. Keeper must commit and compare HEAD:HASH checkpoints itself.

Instrument code_sha256 includes runtime versions (python, lxml, libxml2), so it differs between machines and Actions runners (review C2). Do not use it as a stable identity across runs; pin the lxml version.
PhysicalMaterial is listed in the gate vocabulary but can never be admitted: the pinned semantic pass rejects it under the Immersive wrapper (F1). Weaver or Haiku must not emit it.

The render witness is a placeholder: admission.render is always not_run with required=False. The 'X_ITE render probe' does not exist in this repo; web/app.js renders a browser preview only and is not a candidate-bound witness.

generator.py variety is small: the seed only changes one uniform scale and a timer period, so turns within a family look nearly identical (F6). A visibly turning flywheel needs signal-driven family, tier and biome choices, or Weaver-authored fragments.

Placement replay is O(n^2) (L4), and append re-parses every payload (L3). This is fine for hundreds of turns. At about 48 turns a day, the 10,000 cap is reached in roughly 7 months, and verify then takes more than 12 s.

Fragment-only: the world owns Viewpoint, Background, Text, Inline, scripts, textures and URLs; the gate refuses them. 'New X3D fragment' proposals that use those nodes cannot accrete and belong on the x3d.loom path instead.

Hashes are integrity checks, not signatures: the docs say plainly that nothing authenticates a producer or grants Loom acceptance. Keeper's 'hash-chained ledger' inherits this; do not present it as signed provenance.
serve.py is a loopback-only local author server with an owner.key capability. It is not a reusable API for agents; call WorldStore directly instead.

kit/loomkit/grammar.py defaults to ~/Projects/x3d/x3d_mcp/.venv/bin/python (a Mac path). /home/user/x3d_mcp has no .venv, so on GitHub Actions the grammar/meaning witness returns InstrumentError (status error, never pass) until the workflow creates the venv and sets LOOM_FORK.

x3d.s1/x3d_s1/backends.py price and limit constants (0.042 USD/Mtok input, 64k/32k tokens) and the request wire format are for another vendor's 'jev' typed-judge model, not Claude Haiku. Reuse the adapter pattern (injected transport, pinned model id, token pre-estimate), not the numbers.

x3d.brain/tools/judge_render.py looks like a ready render judge, but it calls a paid hosted multimodal model through LOOM_JUDGE_* env vars (project id, URL template, token) and returns 0..10 numeric scores. That breaks the Loom's own rule that model judges flag and never grade (picture.py rejects scores), and it needs a private paid account.
kit/loomkit/sweep.py and the CLI reference kit/profiles/public-sweep.json, but that rules file is not in the repo (kit/profiles has no public-sweep.json), so sweep cannot run as-is.

kit/loomkit/receipt.py verify() checks a single receipt's self-hash only. It does not walk prev links, so a 'hash-chained ledger' still needs a chain walker. And per LEARNINGS-accretion finding 6, a forger who recomputes the hashes still passes (self-consistency is not authorship), so Keeper should publish a checkpoint out of band.
The CLI 'receipt' command (cli.py ~L287) hard-codes budget={'paid_calls':0,'cloud_resources':0}. Keeper must call receipt.build() directly to record real Haiku model_calls and allowance use.

traps.py docstring claims tests in tests/test_traps.py, but that file does not exist. The trap rules are tested inside kit/tests/test_gates.py instead (15 rules, 88 negative controls, both -O modes, passed when re-run in a scratch copy). Running test_gates.py in place rewrites kit/tests/last-run.json, so run it in a copy.

runs/foldbacks-20261104/report.json and runs/traps-corpus-20261103/report.json are one-off evidence from a Mac (homebrew interpreters, ~/Projects paths, private project zips). They are useful as examples of the report shape, not as reusable fixtures: the incoming/unpacked corpus they read is not in the repo.

kit/examples/hep/render pins X_ITE 16.5.1, x3d.accrete bundles 16.6.0, and many traps.py rules are labelled 'X_ITE 16.5.1'. A runtime-labelled trap must not be promoted to a universal X3D rule, and the probe pin should match the world's runtime.
x3d.s1 ReplayBackend/StubBackend outputs and the Decision Observatory's probabilities are synthetic and authored, not measurements. Never count them as an admitted witness or as calibration evidence.
LOOM-v1.md section 9.1/9.3 (Gobbler, Village Voice, Gobblering with pairwise model votes) is roadmap, explicitly S/L and 'not yet run'. It is design input, not code to call.

The local Python has mcp 2.x installed, where mcp.server.fastmcp no longer exists. src/server.py and every src/tools/*.py module fail to import, and tests/test_hints.py, test_scene_brief.py, test_scene_evidence.py and test_playground_core.py error at collection. Agents must import validation.* and x3d_utils.* directly and never tools.*, or pin mcp<2 (pyproject says >=1.29,<2).

playground/llm.py, judge.py, loop.py, auth.py and config.py are Vertex AI, OpenAI or Google sign-in plumbing (httpx, service-account tokens, OPENAI_API_KEY, Secret Manager). They need paid keys and do not fit the Haiku-allowance or no-model design. Only report.py, mutate.py and fetch_xite.py are worth copying from playground/.
evaluation/hint_loop_gemini.py needs a Gemini API key. evaluation/exact_fix/results.json (17k lines) is recorded output, not a reusable tool.

By default render_image loads X_ITE from the jsdelivr CDN, and the repo's own CI marks the render job continue-on-error because CDN or network trouble breaks it. Pre-fetch X_ITE with playground/fetch_xite.py and set X3D_MCP_XITE_JS. Playwright plus Chromium is also a large install, so cache it on the 30-minute Actions schedule.

Mixed version scope: validate_xml checks 4.0 or 4.1 XSD per document, but semantic.py always uses the 4.1 X3DUOM and profile vocabulary. The x3d.accrete adapter already records this. Do not label a semantic pass as pure 4.0 certification.

The x3d.accrete vendored subset (vendor/x3d_mcp at b5c9956) contains only validate.py, semantic.py, profile.py, listvalues.py, oversize.py, splat_arrays.py and x3duom.py. Using hints.gate, repair_x3d or autofix needs a refreshed ORIGIN.json plus verified-containment.json and the X3DUOM 4.0 file. The adapter refuses source drift, so adding files is a deliberate re-vendor.

validation/validate.py imports jsonschema at module level even for XML-only validation, so jsonschema must be installed. repair's xsi-namespace path also expects the 'x3d' (x3d.py) package; 1 of 384 tests failed here without it.

Semantic-web tools (scene_rdf, semantic_web, shacl_validate, rdf_infer, ontology_guard) need rdflib, pyshacl and owlrl (not installed here) and run SPARQL under a multiprocessing deadline. They are heavy and the server itself says they are 'never a validity verdict', so they are not useful as the Witness gate.
source_witness is a lexical inspector, not a validator, and scene_evidence's 'verified' only means the quote contains the value. Neither may stand in for the XSD + semantic gate.

Splat tools (tools/splats.py, transfer/spz.py, ply.py, chunk.py) and the blob store (transfer/blobs.py, configured by X3D_MCP_BLOB* environment variables) are server-only and need numpy or zstandard. They are irrelevant to small accreted fragments and start background spill machinery when server.py is imported.

/home/user/x3d_mcp/x3d_duo.ipynb (1.4 MB) and examples/semantic_twins/ (oracle/mcp JSON, eval sets) are demos and recorded evaluations, not callable code. examples/scenes has only 3 seed scenes (doha_qatar, red_sphere, table_scene).
